metadata.title: 5 Things to Know Before the Stock Market Opens on Tuesday

content.text:
Stock futures are pointing to a lower open to kick off the holiday-shortened trading week; oil prices and Treasury yields continue to climb; inflation data, earnings from Oracle, and Apple's annual fall launch event headline a busy week; Novartis shares are tumbling following the latest clinical trial results from the Swiss drugmaker; and Bloom Energy shares are gaining on the news that the company will be one of three added to the S&P 500 later this month. Here's what you need to know today.
Stock Futures Fall to Open Shortened Trading Week
Stock futures are lower this morning after a sluggish finish to last week heading into the Labor Day break. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 were recently down 0.8% and 0.3%, respectively, while Nasdaq futures hovered near unchanged. The major indexes fell on Friday following a hotter-than-expected August jobs report, which renewed fears the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this month to tamp down inflation. Market participants were keeping close tabs on Treasury yields and oil prices, both of which were on the rise (more on that below). Gold futures were down 0.7% at 4,445 an ounce, while bitcoin was trading at $78,200, down from a weekend high of $80,500.
Oil Prices, Treasury Yields Continue Rising
The recent surge in oil prices and Treasury yields, which has weighed on stock market sentiment, has extended into this week. Following a record high Labor Day weekend for gas prices, per AAA, WTI crude oil futures, the U.S. benchmark, were up more than 2% recently at just under $94, at their highest level in more than three months. Rising oil prices are likely to spur further increases at the pump and feed through the economy in other ways. Meanwhile, amid concerns about inflation, rising debt and uncertainty about Fed policy, the yield on the 10-year Treasury, which affects interest rates charged on loans, rose to a new multi-year high of 4.81%, up from 4.79% at Friday's close.
Inflation Data, Oracle Earnings, Apple Event on Deck This Week
The consumer price index report for August highlights a busy week of events that market participants will be watching closely. The report, due Friday morning, will factor into the Fed's decision on interest rates next week, as inflation remains well above the central bank's target. Before that, several companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, notably tech giants Oracle (ORCL) and Adobe (ADBE) after the closing bell on Thursday, and supermarket chain Kroger (KR) early Friday. Apple (AAPL) is set to host its annual fall launch event starting tomorrow, where the tech titan is expected to announce a new slate of iPhones that could include the first foldable iPhone. The event is Apple's first big test under new CEO John Ternus, who took over for Tim Cook at the start of the month.
